messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate observed for EU-serving pool. Error rate ~4.2% over last 5m, latency climbs for requests with seqlen>1024. Paging on-call.

alex: I’m on it. Got the alert, checking dashboards now. Can someone check if there was a config roll in the last 10m? @matt?

matt: No deploys in last 30m. Seeing a sudden spike in mTLS handshake failures to one host group (eu-gpu-4). I'll tail logs and dump kube status.

matt: ```
kubectl get pods -n redwood-eu | grep eu-gpu-4
# several pods Ready 1/1, but restarts on eu-gpu-4-7 show 3 in last 15m
journalctl -u inference-worker | grep "handshake failed" | tail -n 30
```

alex: Ok, looks like a hardware flake on that host group. Temporarily draining and routing traffic away.

alex: Action: cordon + drain eu-gpu-4 nodes, update routing policy to prefer eu-gpu-1/2/3, add fallback route to us-west in 3m if pressure doesn't drop. ETA 5-7m for mitigation.

statusbot: Statuspage draft (auto): "Investigating increased error rates impacting inference in EU region. We are routing traffic and investigating root cause. Customers may experience elevated latencies and intermittent errors."

sarah: Copy for customers needs SLA/credits note? We should avoid promises until impact window is confirmed. But start internal eligibility calc: if sustained >99.9% target missed for any hourly window => credit. Need exact minute boundaries and affected customer list. @finance-bot can help compute.

finance-bot: Will compute once you give start/end times and lists. I can run a per-customer usage delta and generate provisional credit amounts.

alex: Beginning mitigation now. Will post updates every 10m or sooner. Current impact window (start) = 1912345678.

matt: Drain complete for problematic nodes. Error rate dropped to 0.9% now, latency trending down. Hold for one more sample.

jamie: I’ll take handoff in 30 minutes. @alex please post a short summary for next oncall with actions taken and open follow-ups.

alex: Handoff summary for @jamie:
- Incident start: 1912345678
- Root cause: hardware/network handshake failures on eu-gpu-4 host group; suspected NIC firmware bug
- Mitigation: cordoned/drained eu-gpu-4, traffic shifted to eu-gpu-1/2/3; temporary routing to us-west if needed
- Observed effect: 5xx spike ~4.2% -> now 0.9% after drain
- Next actions: monitor for recurrence, escalate to infra for hardware RMA if restarts continue, confirm if any customers hit SLA thresholds, prepare customer notify draft if >15m impact

sarah: For SLA eligibility we need: impacted customers list + per-customer error rate during window. If any customer saw >0.1% error uplift vs baseline and the system missed committed uptime for their SLA period, they will be eligible. Also consider partial credits for tiered plans. I can draft a matrix. @finance-bot hand it off.

finance-bot: Received. Please supply "affected_customers.csv" or query GRPC logs for customer id -> I'll run credit_estimate.py.

paul: I pulled a quick sample of top 20 tenants in EU from logs; 3 tenants saw >2% error rate for 12m contiguous. Uploading list to S3: s3://ops-exports/1912345678/impacted_customers.csv

sarah: Thanks @paul. Running provisional calc now. Rules I’ll use:
- Window: start 1912345678 to provisional end when errors <0.5% for 10m contiguous (currently ongoing)
- SLA target: 99.9% hourly uptime
- Credit formula: min( (downtime_minutes / 60) * monthly_commit, cap 100% ) rounded to nearest dollar

sarah: Preliminary results: 3 customers exceed eligibility threshold. Estimated credit amounts attached in spreadsheet (provisional). I’ll coordinate with billing for final values.

alex: Should we send any customer-facing note now (status page already up)? We might prepare a short proactive template but hold send until window confirmed.

matt: Agree. Statuspage should remain "investigating" -> "degraded" if we confirm >10m impact. Keep header minimal. Example update:
```text
We are investigating elevated error rates impacting the EU inference pool. Engineers have drained the affected hosts and traffic is being routed to healthy capacity. Some requests may still experience intermittent failures or increased latency. We will post another update in 10 minutes.
```

sarah: Draft customer email template (internal):
```text
Hi {CustomerName},

We wanted to let you know we experienced an incident on {Date} that affected inference in the EU region for approximately {X} minutes. During this time, you may have seen intermittent errors or increased latency. We are currently assessing the impact on your usage and whether service credits apply under your SLA. We will follow up with a final assessment and any applicable credits by {Date+3 business days}.

Apologies for the disruption.

— Redwood Inference Ops
```

jamie: Good draft. Add link to customer's recent request ids and a short FAQ line about "Do I need to change anything?" -> "No, no action required". Also attach the provisional credit calc.

sarah: Noted. I’ll prepare customer-specific attachments and route to legal for any phrasing checks for enterprise customers.

finance-bot: After legal sign-off, I can push credits to billing queue. Expected timeline: credits appear on next invoice cycle unless customer requests immediate cash-equivalent.

alex: One more check: do we want to open a postmortem doc? If this is NIC firmware, infra should own RMA and PM should link to postmortem.

matt: Yes, creating a postmortem stub: docs/incidents/1912345678-postmortem.md and assigning infra/pm tags.

paul: I'll notify affected customers list once we have final window and amounts. Holding draft until we confirm end timestamp.

alex: Update: metrics stable for 20m, error rate consistent <0.3%. Marking incident as mitigated. Final window end = 1912345750. Please finish eligibility checks and tag billing.

sarah: Running final calc with window 1912345678 - 1912345750. Generating attachments now, will post results and draft emails within 2h.

jamie: Taking on-call. Leaving this thread open for any late regressions. Thanks all :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: EU inference degraded -> mitigated. Root cause: hardware host group failures (pending infra RMA).
